chunks: Basair al-Darajat: Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan, from al-Iys, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is not a prophet or a successor or a king except that he is found in a book which is with me. No by Allah! the name of Muhammad ibn Abdallah ibn al-Hasan is not in there.

key_terms.بِنْيَان: Prophet (in this context, often referring to the lineage or the prophetic figure)
key_terms.وَصِيّ: Successor (specifically referring to the Imam or designated successor)

ai.seo_question: Who is the specific person whose name is not found in the book of prophets and kings according to Abu Abdillah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Basa’ir al-Darajat*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts that every prophet, successor, and king is inscribed in a divine record with him, yet he emphatically excludes Muhammad ibn Abdallah (the son of al-Hasan al-Mujtaba, often identified as al-Nafs al-Zakiyya) from this list. This exclusion is significant in Shia scholarship as it clarifies his status relative to the infallible Imams, distinguishing him as a prominent figure but not one of the designated successors (Awsiya) possessing the same level of divine authority. The statement underscores the precision of divine knowledge regarding lineage and spiritual rank, reinforcing the concept of *Nass* (designation) in Shia theology.
